def _json_response(answer="42", confidence=0.9, **extra):
    obj = {"answer": answer, "confidence": confidence}
    obj.update(extra)
    return json.dumps(obj)


def _make_call_fn(responses):
    """Return a call_fn that yields responses in order; list items may be
    exceptions (raised), str (returned) or other objects (returned)."""
    calls = []

    def call_fn(prompt):
        calls.append(prompt)
        item = responses[len(calls) - 1]
        if isinstance(item, BaseException):
            raise item
        return item

    call_fn.calls = calls
    return call_fn

        f'"answer": "{answer}", "confidence": {confidence}}}'
    )

    return Attempt(
        raw_text=kw.pop("raw_text", ""),
        answer=kw.pop("answer", "x" if parse_ok else None),
        confidence=kw.pop("confidence", 0.9 if parse_ok else None),
        parse_ok=parse_ok,
        passed_validation=passed_validation,
        call_failed=call_failed,
        **kw,
    )

    assert a.raw_text == "raw"
    assert a.answer == "a"

    assert a.parse_ok is True
    assert a.error is None
    assert a.ambiguous is False
    assert a.interpretations == []
    assert a.chosen_interpretation is None
    assert a.passed_validation is True
    assert a.validation_error is None
    assert a.parsed is None
    assert a.call_failed is False

    assert BoothResult(answer="x", status=UNCERTAIN).ok is False
    assert BoothResult(answer="x", status=BLOCKED).ok is False
    assert BoothResult(answer="x", status=AMBIGUOUS).ok is False

  103 |         )

  106 | @dataclass
  107 | class BoothResult:
  108 |     answer: Optional[str]
  109 |     status: str
  110 |     confidence: Optional[float] = None
  111 |     attempts: List[Attempt] = field(default_factory=list)
  112 |     ambiguous: bool = False
  113 |     interpretations: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)
  114 |     evidence_agreement: Optional[float] = None
  115 |     parsed: Optional[dict] = None
  116 |     reason: Optional[str] = None
  117 |     detail: Optional[str] = None
  118 | 
  119 |     @property
  120 |     def n_attempts(self) -> int:
  121 |         return len(self.attempts)
  122 | 
  123 |     @property
  124 |     def ok(self) -> bool:
  125 |         return self.status in (ACCEPTED, REPAIRED)
  126 | 
  127 |     @property
  128 |     def all_parse_failed(self) -> bool:
  129 |         return bool(self.attempts) and all(not a.parse_ok for a in self.attempts)
  130 | 
  131 |     @property
  132 |     def call_failed(self) -> bool:
  133 |         """True if every attempt failed because call_fn itself failed.
  134 | 
  135 |         Derived from the attempts, same idea as all_parse_failed. A call error
  136 |         and a garbage response both still report method == "parse_failure";
  137 |         use this (or attempt.call_failed) to tell them apart.
  138 |         """
  139 |         return bool(self.attempts) and all(a.call_failed for a in self.attempts)
  140 | 
  141 |     @property
  142 |     def checker_failed(self) -> bool:
  143 |         """True when compare_fn crashed or returned an unusable score."""
  144 |         return self.reason in (COMPARE_FAILED, INVALID_SCORE)
  145 | 
  146 |     @property
  147 |     def method(self) -> str:
  148 |         if self.status == AMBIGUOUS:
  149 |             return "ambiguity"
  150 |         if not self.attempts:
  151 |             return "evidence"
  152 |         if self.all_parse_failed:
  153 |             return "parse_failure"
  154 |         if not self.attempts[-1].passed_validation:
  155 |             return "validation"
  156 |         return "confidence"
  157 | 
  158 |     def unwrap(self) -> str:
  159 |         """Return .answer if the result is ok, otherwise raise BoothRejected.
  160 | 
  161 |         .answer itself stays populated on rejected results, for debugging.
  162 |         """
  163 |         if not self.ok or self.answer is None:
  164 |             raise BoothRejected(self)
  165 |         return self.answer
  166 | 
  167 |     def unwrap_or(self, default: str) -> str:
  168 |         """Like unwrap(), but return `default` instead of raising."""
  169 |         try:
  170 |             return self.unwrap()
  171 |         except BoothRejected:
  172 |             return default
  173 | 
  174 |     def to_dict(self) -> dict:
  175 |         # asdict() on the dataclass would miss the computed properties.
  176 |         return {
  177 |             "answer": self.answer,
  178 |             "status": self.status,
  179 |             "confidence": self.confidence,
  180 |             "attempts": [asdict(a) for a in self.attempts],
  181 |             "ambiguous": self.ambiguous,
  182 |             "interpretations": self.interpretations,
  183 |             "evidence_agreement": self.evidence_agreement,
  184 |             "parsed": self.parsed,
  185 |             "n_attempts": self.n_attempts,
  186 |             "ok": self.ok,
  187 |             "all_parse_failed": self.all_parse_failed,
  188 |             "call_failed": self.call_failed,
  189 |             "method": self.method,
  190 |             "reason": self.reason,
  191 |             "detail": self.detail,
  192 |             "checker_failed": self.checker_failed,

  234 | def _try_json(candidate: str) -> Optional[dict]:
  235 |     try:
  236 |         obj = json.loads(candidate)
  237 |     except (json.JSONDecodeError, TypeError):
  238 |         return None
  239 |     return obj if isinstance(obj, dict) else None
  240 | 
  241 | 
  242 | def _iter_raw_decoded_objects(text: str):
  243 |     """Yield every JSON object that starts at a '{' in the text.
  244 | 
  245 |     The flat regex can't handle braces inside string values, raw_decode can.
  246 |     """
  247 |     decoder = json.JSONDecoder()
  248 |     for idx, ch in enumerate(text):
  249 |         if ch != "{":
  250 |             continue
  251 |         try:
  252 |             obj, _ = decoder.raw_decode(text, idx)
  253 |         except json.JSONDecodeError:
  254 |             continue
  255 |         if isinstance(obj, dict):
  256 |             yield obj
  257 |

  259 | def _parse_response(raw_text: str) -> Attempt:
  260 |     candidates: List[Union[str, dict]] = []
  261 | 
  262 |     stripped = raw_text.strip()
  263 |     if stripped.startswith("{") and stripped.endswith("}"):
  264 |         candidates.append(stripped)
  265 | 
  266 |     lines = [ln.strip() for ln in raw_text.splitlines() if ln.strip()]
  267 |     if lines:
  268 |         candidates.append(lines[-1])
  269 | 
  270 |     candidates.extend(_JSON_RE.findall(raw_text))
  271 |     candidates.extend(_iter_raw_decoded_objects(raw_text))
  272 | 
  273 |     last_reason: Optional[str] = None  # why the last candidate was rejected
  274 | 
  275 |     for candidate in candidates:
  276 |         obj = candidate if isinstance(candidate, dict) else _try_json(candidate)
  277 |         if obj is None:
  278 |             if last_reason is None:
  279 |                 last_reason = "no candidate contained a valid JSON object"
  280 |             continue
  281 | 
  282 |         answer = obj.get("answer")
  283 |         confidence = obj.get("confidence")
  284 |         if answer is None or confidence is None:
  285 |             last_reason = "JSON object is missing the required 'answer' or 'confidence' key"
  286 |             continue
  287 | 
  288 |         # Scalars get stringified. dict/list would turn into a repr that
  289 |         # looks like a real answer, so those are rejected.
  290 |         if isinstance(answer, (dict, list)):
  291 |             last_reason = "'answer' was a dict/list, not a scalar value"
  292 |             continue
  293 |         if not isinstance(answer, str):
  294 |             answer = str(answer)
  295 | 
  296 |         if isinstance(confidence, bool):  # bool is an int subclass, so check before float()
  297 |             last_reason = "'confidence' was a boolean, not a number"
  298 |             continue
  299 |         try:
  300 |             confidence = float(confidence)
  301 |         except (TypeError, ValueError):
  302 |             last_reason = f"'confidence' could not be converted to a float: {confidence!r}"
  303 |             continue
  304 |         if not 0.0 <= confidence <= 1.0:
  305 |             last_reason = f"'confidence' {confidence} is out of the [0.0, 1.0] range"
  306 |             continue
  307 | 
  308 |         raw_ambiguous = obj.get("ambiguous", _MISSING)
  309 |         if raw_ambiguous is _MISSING:
  310 |             ambiguous = False
  311 |         else:
  312 |             coerced = _coerce_ambiguous(raw_ambiguous)
  313 |             if coerced is None:
  314 |                 last_reason = f"'ambiguous' had an unrecognized value: {raw_ambiguous!r}"
  315 |                 continue
  316 |             ambiguous = coerced
  317 | 
  318 |         # A blank answer is fine when ambiguous, the interpretations carry the content.
  319 |         if not ambiguous and not answer.strip():
  320 |             last_reason = "'answer' was empty or whitespace-only"
  321 |             continue
  322 | 
  323 |         interpretations = obj.get("interpretations") or []
  324 |         if not isinstance(interpretations, list):
  325 |             interpretations = []
  326 |         interpretations = [str(i) for i in interpretations]
  327 |         chosen = obj.get("chosen_interpretation")
  328 |         chosen = str(chosen) if chosen is not None else None  # keep falsy values like 0
  329 | 
  330 |         return Attempt(
  331 |             raw_text=raw_text,
  332 |             answer=answer,
  333 |             confidence=confidence,
  334 |             parse_ok=True,
  335 |             ambiguous=ambiguous,
  336 |             interpretations=interpretations,
  337 |             chosen_interpretation=chosen,
  338 |             parsed=obj,
  339 |         )
  340 | 
  341 |     return Attempt(
  342 |         raw_text=raw_text,
  343 |         answer=None,
  344 |         confidence=None,
  345 |         parse_ok=False,
  346 |         error=last_reason or "no JSON object could be extracted from the response",
  347 |     )

  350 | def _is_boolish(value) -> bool:
  351 |     """Native bool or a numpy bool, matched by name so numpy isn't imported."""
  352 |     if isinstance(value, bool):
  353 |         return True
  354 |     t = type(value)
  355 |     return t.__module__ == "numpy" and t.__name__ in ("bool_", "bool")

  358 | def _run_validator(
  359 |     validator: Optional[ValidatorFn], answer: Optional[str]
  360 | ) -> Tuple[bool, Optional[str]]:
  361 |     """Run the validator. Returns (passed, error_message).
  362 | 
  363 |     Accepts bool, (bool, str), (bool, None), or the list form of either tuple.
  364 |     """
  365 |     if validator is None or answer is None:
  366 |         return True, None
  367 |     try:
  368 |         result = validator(answer)
  369 |     except Exception as e:
  370 |         return False, f"Validator raised {type(e).__name__}: {e}"
  371 | 
  372 |     if inspect.iscoroutine(result):
  373 |         result.close()  # avoids a "never awaited" warning
  374 |         return False, (
  375 |             "Validator returned a coroutine — validator must be "
  376 |             "synchronous. If your check needs to await something, "
  377 |             "resolve it before calling check()/acheck() and pass a "
  378 |             "plain sync function."
  379 |         )
  380 | 
  381 |     if _is_boolish(result):
  382 |         passed = bool(result)
  383 |         return passed, (None if passed else "Validator returned False")
  384 | 
  385 |     if isinstance(result, (tuple, list)) and len(result) == 2:
  386 |         passed, message = result
  387 |         if _is_boolish(passed) and (message is None or isinstance(message, str)):
  388 |             passed = bool(passed)
  389 |             if message is None:
  390 |                 message = None if passed else "Validator returned False (no message provided)"
  391 |             return passed, message
  392 | 
  393 |     return False, (
  394 |         f"Validator returned an invalid type: {type(result).__name__} "
  395 |         f"(expected bool or (bool, str))"
  396 |     )

  399 | def _evaluate(
  400 |     attempts: List[Attempt],
  401 |     attempt: Attempt,
  402 |     attempt_index: int,
  403 |     threshold: float,
  404 | ) -> Optional[BoothResult]:
  405 |     """Return a final result for this attempt, or None to keep going."""
  406 |     if attempt.parse_ok and attempt.ambiguous:
  407 |         return BoothResult(
  408 |             answer=attempt.answer,
  409 |             status=AMBIGUOUS,
  410 |             confidence=attempt.confidence,
  411 |             attempts=attempts,
  412 |             ambiguous=True,
  413 |             interpretations=attempt.interpretations,
  414 |             parsed=attempt.parsed,
  415 |         )
  416 | 
  417 |     if attempt.parse_ok and not attempt.passed_validation:
  418 |         return None
  419 | 
  420 |     if attempt.parse_ok and attempt.confidence is not None and attempt.confidence >= threshold:
  421 |         status = ACCEPTED if attempt_index == 0 else REPAIRED
  422 |         return BoothResult(
  423 |             answer=attempt.answer,
  424 |             status=status,
  425 |             confidence=attempt.confidence,
  426 |             attempts=attempts,
  427 |             parsed=attempt.parsed,
  428 |         )
  429 | 
  430 |     return None

  433 | def _next_prompt(original_prompt: str, attempt: Attempt) -> str:
  434 |     if attempt.call_failed:
  435 |         # Nothing came back to comment on, so just ask again.
  436 |         return _build_prompt(original_prompt)
  437 |     if not attempt.parse_ok:
  438 |         return _build_parse_failure_prompt(original_prompt, attempt)
  439 |     if not attempt.passed_validation:
  440 |         return _build_validation_failure_prompt(original_prompt, attempt)
  441 |     return _build_retry_prompt(original_prompt, attempt)

  444 | def _finalize_uncertain(attempts: List[Attempt]) -> BoothResult:
  445 |     last_ok = next((a for a in reversed(attempts) if a.parse_ok), None)
  446 |     return BoothResult(
  447 |         answer=last_ok.answer if last_ok else None,
  448 |         status=UNCERTAIN,
  449 |         confidence=last_ok.confidence if last_ok else None,
  450 |         attempts=attempts,
  451 |         parsed=last_ok.parsed if last_ok else None,
  452 |     )

  455 | def _validate_args(threshold: float, max_retries: int) -> None:
  456 |     if not 0.0 <= threshold <= 1.0:
  457 |         raise ValueError(f"threshold must be between 0.0 and 1.0, got {threshold}")
  458 |     if not isinstance(max_retries, int):
  459 |         raise TypeError(f"max_retries must be an int, got {type(max_retries).__name__}")
  460 |     if max_retries < 0:
  461 |         raise ValueError(f"max_retries must be >= 0, got {max_retries}")
  462 |

  464 | def _validate_call_args(prompt, call_fn) -> None:
  465 |     if not isinstance(prompt, str):
  466 |         raise TypeError(f"prompt must be a str, got {type(prompt).__name__}")
  467 |     if not callable(call_fn):
  468 |         raise TypeError(f"call_fn must be callable, got {type(call_fn).__name__}")
  469 | 
  470 | 
  471 | def _validate_on_attempt_callable(on_attempt) -> None:
  472 |     # Fail before any LLM call is spent.
  473 |     if on_attempt is not None and not callable(on_attempt):
  474 |         raise TypeError(f"on_attempt must be callable, got {type(on_attempt).__name__}")
  475 |

  477 | def _validate_evidence_args(evidence_threshold: float) -> None:
  478 |     # bool is rejected here (unlike max_retries): True/False as a threshold is almost certainly a mistake.
  479 |     if isinstance(evidence_threshold, bool) or not isinstance(evidence_threshold, (int, float)):
  480 |         raise TypeError(
  481 |             f"evidence_threshold must be a real number, got {type(evidence_threshold).__name__}"
  482 |         )
  483 |     if not 0.0 <= evidence_threshold <= 1.0:
  484 |         raise ValueError(
  485 |             f"evidence_threshold must be between 0.0 and 1.0, got {evidence_threshold}"
  486 |         )
  487 |

  489 | def _is_empty_evidence(evidence) -> bool:
  490 |     # len() instead of `not evidence`, which raises for multi-element numpy arrays.
  491 |     try:
  492 |         return len(evidence) == 0
  493 |     except TypeError:
  494 |         return not evidence

  497 | def check_with_evidence(
  498 |     answer: str,
  499 |     evidence: Sequence[str],
  500 |     compare_fn: CompareFn,
  501 |     evidence_threshold: float = DEFAULT_THRESHOLD,
  502 | ) -> BoothResult:
  503 |     _validate_evidence_args(evidence_threshold)
  504 | 
  505 |     if answer is not None and not isinstance(answer, str):
  506 |         raise TypeError(f"answer must be a str, got {type(answer).__name__}")
  507 | 
  508 |     if not answer or not answer.strip():
  509 |         return BoothResult(
  510 |             answer=None, status=UNCERTAIN, confidence=None,
  511 |             reason=EMPTY_ANSWER, detail="answer was empty or whitespace-only",
  512 |         )
  513 |     if _is_empty_evidence(evidence):
  514 |         return BoothResult(
  515 |             answer=answer, status=UNCERTAIN, confidence=None,
  516 |             reason=NO_EVIDENCE, detail="evidence sequence was empty",
  517 |         )
  518 | 
  519 |     try:
  520 |         raw_result = compare_fn(answer, evidence)
  521 |     except Exception as e:
  522 |         return BoothResult(
  523 |             answer=answer, status=UNCERTAIN, confidence=None,
  524 |             reason=COMPARE_FAILED, detail=f"{type(e).__name__}: {str(e)[:200]}",
  525 |         )
  526 | 
  527 |     # An async compare_fn just hands back a coroutine instead of raising.
  528 |     if inspect.iscoroutine(raw_result):
  529 |         raw_result.close()
  530 |         raise TypeError(
  531 |             "compare_fn must be synchronous and return bool or float "
  532 |             "directly, not a coroutine. check_with_evidence() does "
  533 |             "not support an async compare_fn."
  534 |         )
  535 | 
  536 |     # Booleans are strict pass/fail, so evidence_threshold doesn't apply to them.
  537 |     if _is_boolish(raw_result):
  538 |         passed = bool(raw_result)
  539 |         score = 1.0 if passed else 0.0
  540 |         block_detail = None if passed else "compare_fn returned False"
  541 |     else:
  542 |         try:
  543 |             score = float(raw_result)
  544 |         except (TypeError, ValueError):
  545 |             return BoothResult(
  546 |                 answer=answer, status=UNCERTAIN, confidence=None,
  547 |                 reason=INVALID_SCORE,
  548 |                 detail=f"compare_fn returned a non-numeric value: {raw_result!r}",
  549 |             )
  550 |         if not 0.0 <= score <= 1.0:
  551 |             return BoothResult(
  552 |                 answer=answer, status=UNCERTAIN, confidence=None,
  553 |                 reason=INVALID_SCORE,
  554 |                 detail=f"compare_fn returned {score}, outside the [0.0, 1.0] range",
  555 |             )
  556 |         passed = score >= evidence_threshold
  557 |         block_detail = (
  558 |             None if passed
  559 |             else f"score {score} below evidence_threshold {evidence_threshold}"
  560 |         )
  561 | 
  562 |     status = ACCEPTED if passed else BLOCKED
  563 |     return BoothResult(
  564 |         answer=answer,
  565 |         status=status,
  566 |         confidence=score,
  567 |         evidence_agreement=score,
  568 |         reason=None if passed else EVIDENCE_DISAGREES,
  569 |         detail=block_detail,
  570 |     )

  602 | def check(
  603 |     call_fn: Callable[[str], str],
  604 |     prompt: str,
  605 |     threshold: float = DEFAULT_THRESHOLD,
  606 |     max_retries: int = DEFAULT_MAX_RETRIES,
  607 |     on_attempt: Optional[Callable[[int, Attempt], Any]] = None,
  608 |     *,
  609 |     validator: Optional[ValidatorFn] = None,
  610 | ) -> BoothResult:
  611 |     _validate_call_args(prompt, call_fn)
  612 |     _validate_args(threshold, max_retries)
  613 |     if _is_async_callable(call_fn):
  614 |         raise TypeError(
  615 |             "check() requires a synchronous call_fn. Use acheck() for "
  616 |             "an async call_fn (async def ... -> str, or an object "
  617 |             "with an async def __call__)."
  618 |         )
  619 |     _validate_on_attempt_callable(on_attempt)
  620 |     if on_attempt is not None and _is_async_callable(on_attempt):
  621 |         raise TypeError(
  622 |             "check() cannot await an async on_attempt callback. "
  623 |             "Use acheck() with an async on_attempt, or pass a sync "
  624 |             "callback to check()."
  625 |         )
  626 | 
  627 |     attempts: List[Attempt] = []
  628 |     current_prompt = _build_prompt(prompt)
  629 | 
  630 |     for i in range(max_retries + 1):
  631 |         try:
  632 |             raw = call_fn(current_prompt)
  633 |         except Exception as e:
  634 |             attempt = _attempt_from_call_error(e)
  635 |         else:
  636 |             bad_return = _call_fn_to_attempt(raw)
  637 |             attempt = bad_return if bad_return is not None else _parse_response(raw)
  638 | 
  639 |         if attempt.parse_ok and not attempt.ambiguous:
  640 |             passed, err = _run_validator(validator, attempt.answer)
  641 |             attempt.passed_validation = passed
  642 |             attempt.validation_error = err
  643 | 
  644 |         if on_attempt is not None:
  645 |             on_attempt(i, attempt)
  646 |         attempts.append(attempt)
  647 | 
  648 |         result = _evaluate(attempts, attempt, i, threshold)
  649 |         if result is not None:
  650 |             return result
  651 | 
  652 |         current_prompt = _next_prompt(prompt, attempt)
  653 | 
  654 |     return _finalize_uncertain(attempts)

  657 | async def acheck(
  658 |     call_fn: Callable[[str], Awaitable[str]],

  662 |     on_attempt: Optional[
  663 |         Union[Callable[[int, Attempt], Any], Callable[[int, Attempt], Awaitable[Any]]]

  665 |     *,
  666 |     validator: Optional[ValidatorFn] = None,

  668 |     _validate_call_args(prompt, call_fn)

  672 |             "or an object with an async def __call__). Use check() for "
  673 |             "a synchronous call_fn."

  675 |     _validate_args(threshold, max_retries)
  676 |     _validate_on_attempt_callable(on_attempt)  # sync or async is decided per call below
  677 | 
  678 |     attempts: List[Attempt] = []
  679 |     current_prompt = _build_prompt(prompt)

  681 |     for i in range(max_retries + 1):
  682 |         try:
  683 |             raw = await call_fn(current_prompt)

    obj = {"answer": answer, "confidence": confidence}
    if ambiguous is not None:

    if interpretations is not None:

    if chosen is not None:
        obj["chosen_interpretation"] = chosen
    return json.dumps(obj)


def static_call_fn(text, n=None):
    """Returns a call_fn that always returns `text`."""
    calls = []

    return fn

import asyncio
import json

import pytest

from booth.core import (
    ACCEPTED,
    AMBIGUOUS,

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _response(**overrides):
    base = {
        "ambiguous": False,
        "interpretations": [],
        "chosen_interpretation": None,
        "answer": "42",
        "confidence": 0.9,
    }
    base.update(overrides)
    return json.dumps(base)


def _make_attempt(parse_ok=True, confidence=0.9, answer="42", **kw):
    return Attempt(
        raw_text="x",
        answer=answer,
        confidence=confidence,
        parse_ok=parse_ok,
        **kw,
    )

# Attempt
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_attempt_defaults():
    a = Attempt(raw_text="r", answer="a", confidence=0.5, parse_ok=True)
    assert a.error is None
    assert a.ambiguous is False
    assert a.interpretations == []
    assert a.chosen_interpretation is None
    assert a.passed_validation is True
    assert a.validation_error is None
    assert a.parsed is None
    assert a.call_failed is False


def test_attempt_interpretations_are_independent():
    a = Attempt(raw_text="r", answer="a", confidence=0.5, parse_ok=True)
    b = Attempt(raw_text="r", answer="a", confidence=0.5, parse_ok=True)
    a.interpretations.append("x")
    assert b.interpretations == []

def test_booth_result_n_attempts_and_ok():
    r = BoothResult(answer="a", status=ACCEPTED)

    assert r.ok is True
    assert BoothResult(answer="a", status=REPAIRED).ok is True
    assert BoothResult(answer="a", status=UNCERTAIN).ok is False
    assert BoothResult(answer="a", status=BLOCKED).ok is False
    assert BoothResult(answer="a", status=AMBIGUOUS).ok is False


def test_all_parse_failed_property():
    assert BoothResult(answer=None, status=UNCERTAIN).all_parse_failed is False
    all_bad = BoothResult(
        answer=None, status=UNCERTAIN,
        attempts=[_make_attempt(parse_ok=False), _make_attempt(parse_ok=False)],
    )
    assert all_bad.all_parse_failed is True
    mixed = BoothResult(
        answer=None, status=UNCERTAIN,
        attempts=[_make_attempt(parse_ok=False), _make_attempt(parse_ok=True)],
    )
    assert mixed.all_parse_failed is False


def test_call_failed_property():
    assert BoothResult(answer=None, status=UNCERTAIN).call_failed is False
    r = BoothResult(
        answer=None, status=UNCERTAIN,
        attempts=[

            _make_attempt(parse_ok=False, call_failed=True),
        ],
    )
    assert r.call_failed is True
    r2 = BoothResult(

    assert r2.call_failed is False


def test_checker_failed_property():

    assert BoothResult(answer=None, status=UNCERTAIN, reason=INVALID_SCORE).checker_failed

    assert not BoothResult(answer=None, status=UNCERTAIN).checker_failed
